scope: Four-word first printed Fatiha ayah,18 embedded Arabic marks,5 upper shapes and native stop/verse ending in actual HTML. Not entire Fatiha.
sourceComparison: Actual native glyphs restore observed wedge sukuns, source body proportions and joins, ba-dot/kasra separation and nun-dot-in-bowl relationships. Five top shapes and native vertically arranged stop/rosette1 are present. No missing/added in-scope body component or tofu was observed at source resolution.

limitations: Four whole-word contexts only; subsequent words, basmala and title still use other fonts and are visibly different.
Source contour font approximates thresholded raster edges, not recovered publisher outlines or100percent scan identity.
Upper marks preserve observed word-local source coordinates. This does not certify Unicode letter identity or instructional span.
Native shaping ligatures retain real Arabic text; partial-character caret behavior is not certified.
Outside scoped firstayah, collision-withheld marks and incomplete allQuran data remain.
Original page bands/decorative furniture and complete global page spacing are not reproduced by this narrow fix.
